did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel chapter 25 is a collection of prophecies of doom against Israel’s neighboring nations: Ammon, Moab and Seir, Edom, and the Philistines.
Did you know? The Ammonites are rebuked because they rejoiced over three tragic events: the desecration of the Temple, the desolation of the land of Israel, and the exile of the house of Judah.
Did you know? The punishment decreed for Ammon includes handing over its land to the “people of the East,” who would live there in tents and enjoy its produce and pasture.
Did you know? Ezekiel describes Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, as destined to become a “pasture for camels,” and the Ammonites’ land as a resting place for flocks.
Did you know? The purpose of Ammon’s punishment, as repeatedly stated in the prophecy, is that they may know that the LORD is God.
Did you know? Moab and Seir claimed that the house of Judah had become like all the other nations, and the prophecy presents this statement as the background to Moab’s coming punishment.
Did you know? The prophecy against Moab mentions the border cities of the land, including Beth-jeshimoth and Baal-meon, as cities that would be breached and handed over to the people of the East.
Did you know? Edom is accused of taking revenge on the house of Judah, so the prophecy describes its devastation and the removal of both people and animals from it.

Did you know? According to the prophecy, the LORD’s vengeance against Edom would be carried out by the people of Israel, who would act against Edom in accordance with the anger and wrath described in the verse.
Did you know? The Philistines are described as having acted against Israel out of revenge, contempt, and enduring hatred, and so the LORD’s hand is turned against them as well.
